elements.requirement: Under section 53A of the Sale of Goods Act 1979, the measure of damages for a seller's breach of contract is the estimated loss directly and naturally resulting, in the ordinary course of events, from the breach.
elements.quote: measure of damages for the seller’s breach of contract is the estimated loss directly and naturally resulting, in the ordinary course of events, from the breach

elements.requirement: Where a seller's breach consists of delivering goods that do not meet the quality required by the contract and the buyer retains the goods, the resulting loss is prima facie the difference between the value of the goods at the time of delivery to the buyer and the value they would have had if they had fulfilled the contract.
elements.quote: prima facie the difference between the value of the goods at the time of delivery to the buyer and the value they would have had if they had fulfilled the contract

elements.requirement: Section 53A of the Sale of Goods Act 1979 does not apply to any contract to which Chapter 2 of Part 1 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 applies.
elements.quote: This section does not apply to a contract to which Chapter 2 of Part 1 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 applies

elements.requirement: Section 53A of the Sale of Goods Act 1979 applies exclusively to Scotland.
elements.quote: This section applies to Scotland only.
